intervals.quote: Fermilab — originally called the National Accelerator Laboratory — began operations in Illinois on June 15, 1967.

intervals.label: first accelerator groundbreaking
intervals.note: Groundbreaking for the linac, the first machine of the complex; no end date given by the source. Recorded as a phase annotation: the source gives the groundbreaking date but no completion, so it marks a milestone rather than an ongoing state.
intervals.quote: the lab broke ground for its first accelerator on Dec. 1, 1968.

name: Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory
notes: Automated requests to www.fnal.gov and history.fnal.gov were refused with HTTP 403 when first tried (2026-09-16), so history and operator facts are taken from news.fnal.gov, the LBNF/DUNE and PIP-II project sites, the laboratory's Leadership and Organization page and the DUNE TDR. The home page was read in a web browser on 2026-10-25.

operator_text.note: Current operator. DOE awarded the management and operating contract to Fermi Forward Discovery Group, LLC (FFDG): "The successful offeror is Fermi Forward Discovery Group, LLC (FFDG)." and "The new contractor will assume operations effective January 1, 2025" (DOE Office of Science, 1 October 2024). Before that date the contractor was Fermi Research Alliance, LLC (DUNE Far Detector TDR, Vol. I, acknowledgements, PDF p. 2: "Fermilab is managed by Fermi Research Alliance, LLC (FRA), acting under Contract No. DE-AC02-07CH11359."). The DUNE TDR (2020) predates the change of contractor.
operator_text.quote: Fermilab is managed by Fermi Forward Discovery Group for the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science.
operator_text.value: Fermi Forward Discovery Group, LLC (FermiForward) for the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science (since 1 January 2025; Fermi Research Alliance, LLC before)

summary.plain: The United States national laboratory for particle physics, near Chicago. It builds and runs the chain of machines that produce the most intense beams of neutrinos in the world, and it hosts the DUNE experiment.
summary.technical: US DOE accelerator laboratory (Batavia, Illinois) operating the 400 MeV linac, 8 GeV Booster, 8 GeV Recycler and 120 GeV Main Injector, the NuMI and BNB neutrino beamlines, the PIP-II superconducting linac under construction and, until 2011, the Tevatron proton-antiproton collider. Host laboratory for LBNF/DUNE.
